records.researcher_notes: The Illinois EPA published a draft construction permit and project summary in June 2024 for Compass Datacenters ORD I at 3333 Beverly Road in Hoffman Estates. The project summary says the company applied for 205 diesel emergency generators: 200 sets of 2,000 kWe and 5 sets of 1,250 kWe. That adds up to 400 MW plus 6.25 MW, or 406.25 MW, in the draft. The point is the street address from the Census geocoder, so the location is marked approximate. The owner is named as Compass Datacenters ORD I, LLC. A Daily Herald article of September 13, 2023 says a data center developer bought the former Sears campus the day before. That is when the project was announced. The draft permit says the Illinois EPA received the air permit application on November 3, 2023. That is when it reached pre-construction. Demolition of the Sears buildings ran from August 2024 to July 2025. A Daily Herald article of September 6, 2025 says the village issued the construction permit for the first building and the site was changing over to construction that month. So the status is construction. The Illinois EPA then issued the construction permit, number 23110012, and a revised construction permit on February 18, 2026, which is in the Illinois EPA document library under site number 031449AEJ. The revised permit covers 200 sets of 2,000 kWe, 5 sets of 500 kWe and 5 sets of 800 kWe, 406.5 MW in all, so the five 1,250 kWe sets in the draft became five 500 kWe sets and five 800 kWe sets. The unit rows follow the revised permit. The library holds a second copy of the same revised permit filed on August 7, 2026. Start year is not known. The same article says each building takes 14 to 16 months to build, but no source gives an opening date.

records.researcher_notes: The Illinois EPA issued a final construction permit on August 14, 2025 to Aligned Data Centers (EGV) PropCo for 112 diesel emergency generator sets at 50 and 150 NW Point Blvd in Elk Grove Village. The project summary lists 35 sets of 3,000 kWe and 77 more sets of 3,000 kWe with exhaust controls. That adds up to 336 MW. The point is the street address from the Census geocoder, so the location is marked approximate. A permit alone puts the status at pre-construction. I did not find a report that the buildings are under construction or open. Start year is not known. The final permit says the Illinois EPA received the application on May 31, 2024. That is the date the project reached pre-construction. The owner is Aligned Data Centers (EGV) PropCo, the company named on the final Illinois EPA permit of August 14, 2025. It is not yet in the GEM entity list. Its parent company, Aligned Data Centers, is in the list with ID 100002029095.

records.plant_name: Edged DeKalb Project Vector Data Center power station

verifications.note: A WTVO news article of Dec 2, 2025. Says Project Vector by Endeavor Energy's Edged platform would deploy TurboCell natural gas generators in DeKalb, with a City Council vote on Dec 8.
A Daily Chronicle article of November 15, 2025. Reports a 560-acre data center proposed in DeKalb that needs annexation and rezoning by the City Council.
A Daily Chronicle article of November 26, 2025. Names Endeavour Energy and its Edged platform and says Edged proposes natural gas for the data center generators in the interim.
A Daily Chronicle article of December 9, 2025. Says the City Council unanimously approved the data center after a public hearing.

The City of DeKalb development projects list of October 14, 2026. Shows Project Vector annexation, rezoning and concept plan approved December 8, 2025, for four data center buildings and two substations.

The DeKalb City Council agenda for December 8, 2025. Ordinance 2025-050 for Project Vector. Says the TurboCell natural gas generators run until the ComEd substation east of Building 1 is operating, and estimates Building 1 in the fourth quarter of 2027. The summary also says Edged is a division of Endeavour Energy that owns and manages data centers, and that Edged offers the TurboCell generators.

records.researcher_notes: A Daily Chronicle article of November 15, 2025 first reported a 560-acre data center proposed in DeKalb, northeast of Keslinger Road and Route 23. A Daily Chronicle article of November 26, 2025 names it as Project Vector by Edged, the data center platform of Endeavour Energy, and says Edged proposes natural gas for the data center generators in the interim. A WTVO news article of December 2, 2025 says the generators would be TurboCell natural gas units used until ComEd finishes grid upgrades. A Daily Chronicle article of December 9, 2025 says the City Council unanimously approved the data center on December 8, 2025. The city's development projects list of October 14, 2026 shows the annexation, rezoning and concept plan approved that day. A city approval is not a permit, so the status stays announced. The council agenda for December 8, 2025 says the gas generators run until the ComEd substation east of Building 1 is working, and estimates Building 1 in the fourth quarter of 2027. So 2027 is entered as a planned start year. The generators may be removed once grid power arrives. I did not find a megawatt rating, a generator count, an Illinois EPA air permit or a report of a groundbreaking. The point is on Keslinger Road near the named site and is only approximate. The owner is Edged, already in the GEM entity list with ID 100002029103. The city council agenda for December 8, 2025 says Edged is a division of Endeavour Energy that owns and manages data centers, and that Edged supplies the TurboCell generators. The Daily Chronicle article of November 26, 2025 also names Edged as the developer. JJK 343 LLC filed the petition, but it is the landowner and not the plant owner. Endeavour Energy is not in the entity list, and the Edged entity has no parent set. The Endeavor Energy entities in the list are a Texas oil company and are not the same firm. Capacity is blank.
